items.title: What ReStructura is for
items.text: Record what is inside your walls and floors while you renovate: pipes, cables, conduits. Put a **pin** on the plan where something is, then add photos, notes and measurements, so you can find it again before you drill.

items.title: Everything stays on this computer
items.text: No account, no internet, no cloud. Each project is one folder on this computer. You can export it as a single .zip file to back it up or to hand it to someone else.

items.title: Projects
items.text: The app always opens on the **main menu**, which lists your projects: one per home or renovation. Type a name and press **Create** to start a new one. Each project in the list has **Open**, **Rename…**, **Export…** and **Delete**. A deleted project goes to the system trash, so it can be recovered.

items.title: Your first floor
items.text: A new project asks for its first floor. **Import a plan image** (PNG or JPEG: a scan, a photo of the drawing, an export from your architect), or **Draw the plan in the editor** on an empty sheet.

items.title: Moving around the plan
items.text: Scroll to zoom and drag to pan. **Fit view** shows the whole plan again. Right-click anywhere on the plan for a menu of what you can do at that spot.

items.title: Two modes: Document and Draw
items.text: The switch in the header chooses the mode. **Document** is for pins, photos, room names and measurements. **Draw** opens the plan editor for walls, doors and windows.

items.title: Adding a floor
items.text: **Add ▾ → Floor (plan image)…** imports another plan image. **Add ▾ → Floor (draw it)…** starts an empty sheet. A mezzanine or a basement is a floor too.

items.title: Switching and renaming floors
items.text: With two or more floors, the **Floor** list in the header switches between them. The pencil next to it renames the current floor.

items.title: Adding a pin
items.text: **Add ▾ → Pin**, then click the plan. Or right-click the spot and choose **Add pin here**. The pin panel opens on the right.

items.title: What a pin holds
items.text: A **label** (what is here), a **category** (electric power, water, gas and so on, which sets its colour), the **room** it is in, free **notes**, photos and measurements. Everything saves by itself as you type: there is no Save button.

items.title: Photos
items.text: **Attach photos…** copies JPEG, PNG or WebP pictures into the project. Click a photo to see it full size: the arrow keys move between photos, and each one can have a caption. **Remove photo** can be undone. HEIC photos (the iPhone format) cannot be used: convert them to JPEG first. The app says so, in red, if you pick one.

items.title: Measurements
items.text: **Height above floor**, **Depth in wall**, and any number of **Distance from…** a reference you name, for example “left jamb of the kitchen door”. Type a length in any unit: 112, 112 cm, 1.12 m, 44 in, 3' 8".

items.title: Moving a pin
items.text: Pins never move by accident. Press **Edit position** in the pin panel (or right-click the pin), then click where it should go: each click moves it. **Done** or Esc locks it again.

items.title: Several pins at once
items.text: Ctrl+click or Shift+click adds pins to the selection, and Ctrl+A selects every visible pin. Then copy, cut, paste or delete them together. Paste puts the copies at the mouse pointer and keeps their layout. Photos are not copied.

items.title: Pin colours
items.text: Pin colours follow the colour convention chosen in the **legend**: European (the default) or APWA (US). A pin stores what it is, not a colour, so switching convention recolours every pin.

items.title: Naming rooms
items.text: **Add ▾ → Room label**, then click inside the room. Give it a name and, if you like, the ceiling height. Room names appear on the plan and in the printed report.

items.title: Tagging a pin with its room
items.text: In the pin panel, choose the room from the **Room** list. Search and the printed report can then use it.

items.title: Moving or deleting a room label
items.text: Click the label to open it, then **Move label** (and click the new spot) or **Delete label**. Pins tagged with a deleted room simply lose the tag.

items.title: Calibrating a plan
items.text: A plan image has no scale until you give it one. Press **Calibrate** in the bottom bar, click the two ends of something you have measured (one wall is enough) and type its real length. Hold Shift to keep the line horizontal or vertical. The dot in the bottom bar turns green.

items.title: What calibration adds
items.text: A scale bar, the **Measure distance** tool (right-click the plan), measurements kept on the plan, and the distance between two selected pins. Everything else works without it, and lengths typed on a pin never depend on it.

items.title: Measurements kept on the plan
items.text: A measured distance stays on the plan as a dashed line with its length. Click it to select it and press Delete to remove it. Recalibrating updates them all.

items.title: Drawn floors are already to scale
items.text: A floor drawn in the editor is to scale from the start, so it needs no calibration.

items.title: How accurate is it?
items.text: Distances read off a plan are approximate: they depend on how accurately it was drawn, scanned and calibrated. For anything that matters, measure on site and type it on the pin.

items.title: Searching pins
items.text: Ctrl+F or the magnifier in the header. Search looks through labels, notes, rooms and photo captions on every floor, with filters for floor, category, room, photos and measurements. Pins that do not match fade on the plan. Click a result to go to it.

items.title: The legend
items.text: Lists the pin categories with their colours and counts. Click a category to hide or show its pins. The arrow at the top folds the legend down to a small tab.

items.title: The tools
items.text: Draw mode shows a tool palette on the left: **Select** (V), **Wall** (W), **Door** (D), **Window** (N) and **Stairs** (T). The bar at the top shows the options of the current tool.

items.title: Drawing walls
items.text: Choose **Wall** and click corner after corner. Clicks lock onto existing corners and walls, and straighten lines that are nearly horizontal, vertical or at 45°. Hold Ctrl to switch that off. Click the same point twice or press Enter to stop. Backspace takes back the last wall.

items.title: Exact lengths
items.text: While drawing, type a length (350, 3.5 m, 11' 6") and press Enter: the wall gets exactly that length, in the direction of the mouse. A plain number is read in the unit shown next to the box. **Thickness** sets the thickness of the next walls.

items.title: Changing walls
items.text: With **Select**, click a wall (Shift+click adds more). Change its **Length** or **Thickness** in the top bar. To move a corner, click its round handle, then click where it should go: the walls joined there follow.

items.title: Placing doors and windows
items.text: Choose **Door** or **Window** and pick the **Type**. Click on a wall where the opening starts (for a door, the hinge side), then where it ends, or type the width and press Enter. The door opens towards the side of the wall the mouse is on.

items.title: Door and window types
items.text: Doors: single, double, pocket (sliding into the wall) and an opening with no door. Windows: window, French window with one or two leaves, and fixed window. They are drawn with the standard plan symbols a builder recognises.

items.title: Changing a door or window
items.text: With **Select**, click it to change its type, **Width** or distance **From corner**. **Side** (F) makes it open the other way and **Hinge** (H) moves the hinge to the other end. Click it once more to slide it along its wall.

items.title: Stairs
items.text: Choose **Stairs** and pick the **Type**: straight or spiral. Click one corner of the stair's footprint, on the side where it starts, then the opposite corner. A straight stair climbs along its longer side, away from your first click. The number of **Steps** is worked out from the length (about 28 cm per tread) unless you type one. With **Select**: **Reverse** (F) makes it climb or turn the other way, **Up / down** (U) says whether it goes up or down from this floor, and clicking it again moves it. It is drawn with the standard symbol: treads, a walking line from a dot to an arrow, UP or DOWN, and a break line where the plan cuts a stair going up.

items.title: Tracing over a plan image
items.text: On an imported plan, Draw mode first asks you to calibrate it, then shows the image faintly so you can trace the walls. The **Plan image** slider sets how faint.

items.title: The drawing sheet
items.text: A drawn floor starts as a 40 × 30 m sheet with a 1 m grid. Draw past its edge and the sheet grows, always keeping some paper beyond the walls.

items.title: Back to pins
items.text: Pins stay visible while you draw but cannot be clicked. Switch back to **Document** to work with them.

items.title: Exporting a project
items.text: **Export ▾ → Project as a .zip file…** saves the whole project (plans, photos, data) as one file. It is a plain zip: it opens on another computer with ReStructura, and anyone can unzip it to get the photos.

items.title: Importing a project
items.text: On the main menu, **Import project (.zip)…** adds an exported project to your list.

items.title: Printable report (PDF)
items.text: **Export ▾ → Printable report (PDF)…** builds a report: each floor with its numbered pins, room names and scale bar, then each pin with its notes, measurements and photos. Choose the whole project or one floor, with or without photos, then **Open in browser**: the report opens in your web browser, where **Print or save as PDF** at the top prints it or saves it as a PDF file.

items.title: Application settings
items.text: The gear opens **Settings**. Application settings belong to this computer: language, appearance (light, dark or as the system), measurement units, the colour convention for new projects, and where projects are stored.

items.title: Measurement units
items.text: Centimetres, metres, feet and inches, or inches. This only changes what is shown: lengths are always stored in centimetres, and you can type any unit at any time.

items.title: Project settings
items.text: With a project open, Settings also shows the project's name, its colour convention and a summary of what it contains. These travel with the project when you export it.

items.title: Undo and redo
items.text: Every change is one step. Use the arrows in the header, or Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y). While you are typing in a box, Ctrl+Z first undoes the typing.

items.title: The error log
items.text: When something fails, a red message appears and the details are written to a log file on this computer. **Show log file** opens the folder that contains it. Settings shows where it is too.

items.title: Reporting a problem
items.text: Send the log file with a few words about what you were doing. **How to report**, in the red message or in Settings, shows where the file is and where to send it.

items.title: A copy before every update
items.text: When a new version of ReStructura changes how projects are stored, it first keeps a copy of each project's database as it was (for example plan.db.v9.bak, in the project folder). The copy is not included in exports.

items.title: Cancel, close, or step back one level
Add a pin to the selection, or take it out
Delete the selected pins or measurement
Keep a calibration or measuring line straight
Previous or next photo, in the photo viewer
Type an exact length or width while drawing
Door or window: open towards the other side
Door or window: hinge at the other end
Stair: going up or going down
Stop, leave the tool, clear the selection

menu.projects.title: Your projects
menu.projects.text: One project per home. Click a project to open it. Each one can also be exported or deleted from here.

menu.new.title: New project
menu.new.text: Type a name and press Create. Import brings in a project someone exported for you.

menu.help.title: Help, any time
menu.help.text: This button, or F1, opens Help: how everything works, with a search box and every keyboard shortcut. You can replay this tour from there.

menu.settings.title: Settings
menu.settings.text: Language, light or dark appearance, and measurement units: centimetres, metres, or feet and inches.

plan.map.title: The plan
plan.map.text: Scroll to zoom and drag to move around. Right-click anywhere for a menu of what you can do at that spot.

plan.add.title: Add
plan.add.text: Add a pin where something is inside a wall, a room name, or another floor.

plan.mode.title: Document or Draw
plan.mode.text: Document is for pins, photos and measurements. Draw opens the editor for walls, doors and windows.

plan.legend.title: Legend
plan.legend.text: Pin colours by category. Click a category to hide or show its pins. The arrow folds the legend away.

plan.scale.title: Scale
plan.scale.text: Calibrate an imported plan by measuring one wall: the app can then show real distances and a scale bar.

plan.search.title: Search
plan.search.text: Find any pin by its label, notes, room or photo captions, on every floor. Shortcut: Ctrl+F.

plan.export.title: Export
plan.export.text: Save the whole project as one .zip file, or print a report with the plan, the pins and their photos.

plan.undo.title: Undo
plan.undo.text: Every change can be undone and redone, also with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z.

plan.help.title: Help
plan.help.text: Everything else is explained here, with a search box. F1 opens it too.

draw.tools.title: Tools
draw.tools.text: Select (V), Wall (W), Door (D), Window (N) and Stairs (T). Pick one, then click on the plan.

draw.bar.title: Options
draw.bar.text: The options of the current tool. Type exact lengths, widths and thicknesses here: a plain number is read in the unit shown.

draw.plan.title: Drawing
draw.plan.text: Click corner after corner to draw walls. Clicks lock onto corners and walls; hold Ctrl to switch that off. Esc steps back one level at a time.

draw.back.title: Back to pins
draw.back.text: Switch to Document to work with pins, photos and room names again.
